newsitem.title: FRANCE: France "unable to support" Zaire intervention.
newsitem.headline: France "unable to support" Zaire intervention.

text.p: France said on Monday it could not support a plan for three African states to help Kinshasa battle rebels in eastern Zaire because of a European Union embargo on military aid to the region.
"For France, there is an embargo of the European Union. We cannot break an embargo of the European Union," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told Reuters.
France has expressed concern about Zaire's territorial integrity.

Rummelhardt said the EU embargo prevented France from giving even verbal support to a plan announced by Kinshasa on Monday to fly in troops from allies Morocco, Togo and Chad to bolster its army in a war against the rebels.
Rummelhardt spoke after Foreign Minister Herve de Charette met his Zairean counterpart Kamanda Wa Kamanda in Paris.
The Union for Democracy and Social Progress, a Zairean opposition party, said Kamanda was in Paris to promote the intervention plan and urged France to reject it.

Rummelhardt acknowledged Kamanda and de Charette had "discussed the situation in the Great Lakes region" among other topics. He said he did not know whether Zaire's plan to beef up its army with soldiers from other African states had come up.
French officials say there are only five French military staff in the central African country -- the embassy's defence attache and four security guards.
France has urged respect for Zaire's territorial integrity and officials are worried that the rebels' campaign may put Zaire's survival in doubt.
France has advocated creating an African intervention force to help solve regional problems, similar to a rival proposal by Washington.

Tutsi-led rebels have been battling the mercenary-backed Zaire army since October and hold a strip of eastern Zaire extending from the borders with Rwanda and Uganda to Zaire's mineral-rich Shaba province.
Zaire accuses Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of fighting alongside the ethnic Tutsis.
The rebels say their goal is to topple Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, who has ruled Zaire since 1965. Mobutu has ruled out negotiations, vowing to defeat the rebels on the battlefield.
